newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends higher on refiners' buying.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends higher on refiners' buying.

text.p: Palm oil prices in Malaysia ended the day higher after talk of refiners' buying and firm underlying fundamentals helped sentiment, traders said.
"There was some buying from refiners," a trader said.
"There was a lot of support around 1,242 and 1,243 ringgit for March futures but the buying fizzled off thereafter," he said, adding that firm fundamentals also underpinned sentiment.
Talk emerged that output in December fell by an estimated 15 to 18 percent from November. Traders attributed the expected fall to a downward trend in seasonal crops.
"We expect output to fall further in January but we cannot tell the percentage fall right now," another trader said.
"Demand is expected to increase with fresh tenders likely to come into the market after the New Year holidays," he said.
Activity picked up late in the day after the market traded in a tight range in earlier sessions, they said. Turnover rose to 997 lots from Thursday's 554 lots at the close.
But traders said trading was still cautious and sluggish as most players were still away for the year-end holidays.
Among physical, Dec (south) saw offers at 1,272.50 ringgit against bids at 1,267.50 with early trades of 1,265 and 1,270,
Dec (central) was offered at 1,257.50 and bids at 1,252.50. Jan (south) saw offers at 1,272.50 with bids at 1,267.50, Jan (central) at 1,260 with bids at 1,252.50.
Feb (south) was offered at 1,272.50 and bids at 1,260.
Among refined products, Jan RBD palm oil was offered at $532.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Feb/March at $530 and Apr/May/Jun at $530.
Jan RBD palm olein saw offers at $570, Feb/Mar at $567.50 and Apr/May/June at $557.50.
Jan RBD palm stearin was offered at $402.50, Feb/Mar at $405, and Jan/Feb palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $292.50.
Third month March futures closed five ringgit up at 1,241 ringgit ($490.90) a tonne.
